newsitem.title: SPAIN: Prima Air expects to add third aircraft to fleet.
newsitem.headline: Prima Air expects to add third aircraft to fleet.

text.p: Prima Air, a Spanish independent airline, that started operations in March this year, is expecting to take delivery of a third aircraft in the next few months, a company spokesman said.
The airline, based in Santiago de Compostela, in the northwestern province of Galicia, operates two Saab 340 aircraft on four national and two international routes.
A third aircraft will be in service in October, November time, he said.
As well as this, the Spanish airline is considering adding serveral more destinations in northern Spain and Portugal,the spokesman told Reuters.
Cargo and passenger traffic have been doing well' in the first six months of operation, he said.

The operator only carries cargo when the passenger load is not at 100 percent capacity, he said. Prima Air has been taking fruit and fish from Galicia to other parts of Spain such as Alicante and in particular Bilbao, he added.
The airline is owned by a group of Spanish businessmen.
